ai.description: This small frog (25–30 mm) is bright lime-green with scattered white spots. It is distinguished by its translucent belly and distinct, large, horizontally elliptical pupils.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Raorchestes chalazodes* is uniquely distinguished by its translucent, pale-green belly and distinct, bright white spots scattered across its flanks and limbs.
ai.habitat: Raorchestes chalazodes inhabits the evergreen forests of the Western Ghats, typically residing in high-altitude montane rainforests and reed-filled swamps above 1,000 meters.
ai.behavior: Günther's Bush Frog is nocturnal and exhibits a unique defensive strategy by tucking its limbs and remaining motionless to blend into foliage when threatened.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Raorchestes chalazodes* exhibits direct development, laying small clutches of eggs inside bamboo internodes. Breeding occurs during the monsoon season (June–August).
ai.distributionRemarks: Raorchestes chalazodes is endemic to the southern Western Ghats in Kerala and Tamil Nadu, typically found at elevations between 800 and 1,200 meters.
ai.callDescription: The advertisement call of *Raorchestes chalazodes* consists of a series of high-pitched, insect-like "tink" notes emitted from within dense, high-altitude rainforest foliage.
